From: Emily Hudson <emily.hudson@aurelia-analytics.com>

Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Mutual action plan + evaluation seeds and cost assumptions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We had a productive product review internally and would like to start a short MAP focused on (1) functional evaluation, (2) unit-economics sanity checks, and (3) a close timeline. Two asks from our side to kick off:

- Can Redwood confirm the tokens-per-inference assumptions you used during the demo (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens)?
- We want to record expected caching and batching behavior in the MAP so that our finance team can model tokens/$ reliably. In particular: what cache-hit rate should we assume for a prefix cache, and what batching size distribution do you recommend for an initial production workload ~200 rps?

I attached a small evaluation seed (Aurelia_eval_seed_set.csv) with representative prompts. Our acceptance criteria for the eval: p95 latency < 350ms (appl. server -> model), top-1 quality pass rate >= 88% on the seed set. Also trying to align timelines: we'd like a two-week evaluation window starting as soon as next Monday (2026-08-10) and a PO decision by 2026-08-24 if results are good.

Can you confirm availability and whether you need anything else to scope the perf/cost checks?

Thanks,
Emily Hudson
Head of ML Product
Aurelia Analytics

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com

Hi Emily — great to hear the internal review went well. Attaching a draft MAP (MAP-v1-vanessa.docx) and a short perf test plan. Quick answers and assumptions that we will validate during the eval: 

- Demo assumptions (approx): avg prompt = 120 tokens, avg completion = 240 tokens, so ~360 tokens per request. We'll run token-level logging during the eval to confirm.
- Price benchmark used for estimates: $0.00030 per token for the hosted model family used in the demo; we will provide a committed pricing quote for Dedicated if you move to reserved capacity.
- Caching: we typically see 12–18% prefix cache hits for first-pass POC telemetry on this class of workload; for MAP planning assume 15% cache hit unless you have a high repeat-prompt surface. Cache hits are counted as tokens avoided for forward pass but have small metadata overhead.
- Batching: for interactive 200 rps load we model average batching of 4–10 depending on arrival variability; for cost modeling use conservative avg batch size = 6. Batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU overhead and improves tokens/$ but increases tail latency slightly.

Planned MAP milestones (high level):
1) 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-24: evaluation window (functional + perf + unit-econ run)
2) 2026-08-19: interim checkpoint — we share perf and token consumption dashboard
3) 2026-08-24: decision/PO if acceptance criteria met

If that timeline looks good I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with our perf team and engineering to align on instrumentation and the exact model variant (we plan to use redwood-compact-v1-q4 for the evaluation to keep latency/cost tradeoffs realistic).

Notes: I quoted tokens per token pricing conservatively; we will produce a final tokens/$ projection during the MAP after we ingest your seed set and run the perf suite.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa — quick ops note to include in the MAP:

- We'll run two perf vectors: single-request latency (no batching) and production-like batching at avg size 6. I'll push perf-test-plan.md to the shared Drive folder today.
- Quantization/variant: redwood-compact-v1-q4 gives ~1.7x speedup vs float32 for autoregressive workloads without material quality drop in our internal evals; we'll record any deltas in the acceptance report.
- KV/prefix caching behavior: we'll instrument cache-hit ratio and token-savings metric. Please make sure Aurelia can route a small fraction (5%) of traffic to the evaluation endpoint for realtime logs if they want live dashboards.

On the cost side, I'll produce a tokens/$ sensitivity table during the run (varying cache hit 5–25% and avg batch size 2–8).

Emily — thanks for the clear asks. Finalizing the MAP doc now and copying the key MAP action items here so procurement/finance have a single view: 

MAP action items (finalized for eval):
- Eval window: 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-24 (two-week run).
- Model variant: redwood-compact-v1-q4 (instrumented); can run a float32 baseline on request.
- Token assumptions (initial): avg request = 360 tokens (120 prompt / 240 completion). We'll surface exact averages after ingesting the seed set.
- Cost assumptions for MAP budgeting (ballpark for planning): $0.00030 per token *expected published demo rate*; two-week eval on 200 rps traffic sampled at 10% = ~1.7M tokens/day -> ~US$510/day -> ~US$7,140 for two weeks. This is a planning number; final tokens/$ and total will be adjusted after real token counts and cache-hit data are collected.
- Caching assumption: assume 15% prefix cache hit (sensitivity 5–25%). Cache hit reduces billed tokens; we'll include a token-savings column per run.
- Batching assumption: avg batch size = 6 for production-like run; we will also test avg batch sizes 2 and 8 during perf vectors.
- Deliverables at end of eval: token-level logs (daily), cache-hit/time series, latency (p50/p95/p99), quality report against seed set with pass rate, and tokens/$ sensitivity table across cache and batching scenarios.
- Acceptance criteria: quality >= 88% on seed pass rate AND p95 model latency (appl -> model) < 350ms.

Next steps: I will upload the MAP-v1 document to the Drive and schedule the 30-min kickoff for 2026-08-10 11:00 AM ET (meeting invite to follow). Rishi will run the perf vectors and share the interim dashboard on 2026-08-19.

If Aurelia is good with the eval-spend ballpark we quoted above, we can accept a short-form PO to enable the evaluation infra. If procurement needs a revised cost target (tokens/$) we can update prior to the kickoff.

Attachments: MAP-v1-vanessa.docx, perf-test-plan.md
